sourceCheck:
Verified on 2026-10-08. The [AI-102 study guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/ai-102) and [retired-exam list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/support/retired-certification-exams) confirm AI-102 retired June 30, 2026. Microsoft's [replacement announcement](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/skills-hub-blog/the-ai-job-boom-is-here-are-you-ready-to-showcase-your-skills/4494128) was opened, but its original dynamic body was not extractable; indexed excerpts of the Microsoft-authored article identify the AI-103 successor, and community replies were excluded as evidence. The [current certification page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/azure-ai-apps-and-agents-developer-associate/) names Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate. The [AI-103 guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/ai-103) names Exam AI-103: Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure and skills measured April 16, 2026. Every measured objective bullet was read. Its five weights are 25–30%, 30–35%, 10–15%, 10–15%, and 10–15%; its fourteen groups match the supplied headings and order. No newer outline or AI-103 retirement notice appeared. Section numbering is editorial; Study resources do not expand scope.
[Foundry overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/what-is-foundry) confirms Microsoft Foundry and Foundry Tools, with Responses, conversations, and versioned agents distinct from classic Assistants, threads, and runs. The [SDK reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/sdk-overview) establishes stable azure-ai-projects 2.x, the 2.3.0 baseline, and OpenAI Python 3.x. Project endpoints, direct model endpoints, and tool-specific endpoints are separate; project endpoints currently do not route embeddings. [Azure OpenAI v1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/api-version-lifecycle) uses OpenAI() base_url, deployment identifiers in model, and GA requests with no dated api-version requirement. [Current Foundry RBAC names](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry) preserve the renamed roles' IDs and core permissions.
[Feature-specific availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/general-availability) governs coverage: portal GA does not establish GA for every component. Foundry Workflows is preview and retires December 1, 2026; the plan uses supported code orchestration. Agent memory, agent guardrail interventions, preview monitoring surfaces, experimental client instrumentation, preview evaluators, and preview model leaderboards are excluded. Prompt-agent server-side tracing and supported GA model controls remain in scope. The [reasoning reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/reasoning) supports model-specific controls and summaries, not access to hidden reasoning. Conflicting model-version dates and uncorroborated GA examples are excluded.
[Content Understanding release notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-understanding/whats-new) establish 2025-11-01 as the GA API. The guide's pro-mode objective refers to retired 2025-05-01-preview; [agentic mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-understanding/concepts/agentic-mode) uses 2026-06-01-preview and is not a drop-in replacement. Pro-mode and agentic-mode implementation coverage is excluded; supported GA analyzers supply the extraction cards.
The [image guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/dall-e) and [retirement schedule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule) confirm DALL-E 3 retired March 4, 2026 and GPT-Image-2, GPT-Image-2.5-Flare, and GPT-Image-2.5-Sunburst are GA. Section 3.1 retains its official heading but tests supported image generation and editing: [Sora 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/video-generation) remains preview, its current version retires October 15, 2026, and no GA video alternative was verified. Conflicting image transparency, WEBP, default-quality, and legacy route examples are excluded.
Additional conflicts and gaps: the [guardrail overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview) contradicts itself about severity-threshold direction, so that distinction is excluded. [Standard custom categories](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/concepts/custom-categories) list retirement on September 1, 2026; rapid custom categories, joint image-plus-text analysis, and the current [provenance-detection API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/content-safety/provenance-disclosure) are preview; arbitrary brand/prohibited-symbol classification and those calls are excluded. Signed-provenance behavior remains covered. Language documentation has inconsistent NER version labeling; the plan uses its explicitly GA parameter reference. Speech and Realtime examples mix historical and current shapes; planned cards use GA Speech behavior and Azure OpenAI v1 Realtime event contracts. Current component references, rather than stale samples or renamed terminology, determine each card's behavior.

cards.statement: An engineer selects file search for managed chunking of product manuals uploaded to a Foundry agent.
cards.explanation: File search chunks uploaded files during managed ingestion, reducing the document-preparation code the developer maintains.

cards.statement: Grounding with Bing Search can give application developers raw search-tool output for their own processing.
cards.explanation: Foundry Agent Service returns model-generated answers from Bing grounding, rather than exposing the raw search-tool output.
cards.misconception: Bing grounding exposes raw search results to the application.

source.title: Use Grounding with Bing Search tools

cards.statement: For calculations over an uploaded CSV, an engineer selects Code Interpreter for a Foundry agent.
cards.explanation: Code Interpreter runs Python in a managed sandbox to analyze attached data files.

cards.statement: An Azure AI Search vectorizer generates document embeddings during an indexer's ingestion pipeline.
cards.explanation: An Azure AI Search vectorizer converts query input to vectors at query time. Indexing uses embedding skills.
cards.misconception: A vectorizer performs the embedding skill's indexing job.

source.title: Integrated vector embedding in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: For schema-shaped metadata from videos, an engineer selects Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools.
cards.explanation: Content Understanding lets an engineer configure video analyzers to return custom fields from visual and audio evidence.
tags: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools

cards.statement: An engineer adds image understanding to a deployed Azure OpenAI model by creating a Foundry connection.
cards.explanation: Image captioning needs a vision-enabled model deployment. A Foundry connection does not change the deployed model's input capabilities.
cards.misconception: A project connection adds a new input modality to the deployed model.

cards.statement: An engineer evaluates Azure OpenAI reasoning models for a coding app that needs complex code generation.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI reasoning models target advanced coding and problem-solving tasks, making task-specific evaluation useful for selection.

cards.statement: An engineer chooses fine-tuning to keep a Foundry app grounded in inventory records that change throughout the day.
cards.explanation: RAG retrieves changing records for grounding. Fine-tuning targets model behavior or task performance rather than adding fresh knowledge.
cards.misconception: Fine-tuning is the retrieval method for frequently changing facts.

cards.statement: An engineer selects an Azure AI Search indexer to ingest Azure Blob Storage files on a recurring schedule.
cards.explanation: An indexer pulls from a supported data source and refreshes the target index on a configured schedule.

cards.statement: For a Chat Completions coding app, an engineer selects a gpt-5.1-codex deployment in Azure OpenAI.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.1-codex uses the Responses API. A Chat Completions app needs a compatible model or an API migration.
cards.misconception: A coding model supports the application's existing Chat Completions API.
cards.volatilityNote: Model-specific API support and model availability can change.

cards.statement: For Global Standard, Azure stores model data at rest in the designated Azure geography.
cards.explanation: Global Standard keeps stored data in its designated geography; its deployment type governs inference processing separately.

cards.statement: With Data Zone Standard, Azure confines inference processing to the Foundry resource's Azure region.
cards.explanation: Data Zone Standard routes inference within the specified Microsoft data zone, which can include multiple Azure regions.
cards.misconception: A data zone deployment pins inference to one region.

cards.statement: For steady high-volume model traffic, an engineer uses Global Provisioned to reserve processing capacity.
cards.explanation: Global Provisioned reserves model processing capacity through provisioned throughput units for predictable throughput.

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 caller requires a monthly api-version value when submitting a Responses request.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI v1 removes the requirement for a dated api-version query parameter in GA requests.
cards.misconception: Azure OpenAI v1 keeps the dated API-version requirement.

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 developer sets OpenAI() base_url to the resource endpoint ending in /openai/v1/.
cards.explanation: The OpenAI Python client targets Azure OpenAI v1 through base_url, including the /openai/v1/ route.

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 caller uses the catalog model name in model after renaming its Azure deployment.
cards.explanation: The model argument identifies the Azure deployment. A renamed deployment needs its configured deployment name in the call.
cards.misconception: The catalog model name overrides an Azure deployment's chosen name.

cards.statement: With azure-ai-projects 2.3.0, AIProjectClient requires a Foundry project endpoint for project operations.
cards.explanation: AIProjectClient connects to the endpoint containing /api/projects/<project-name> for Foundry project operations.

cards.statement: With azure-ai-projects 2.3.0, a developer sends embeddings.create requests through the project endpoint.
cards.explanation: Embedding requests go to the direct Azure OpenAI model endpoint. The Foundry project endpoint currently does not route embeddings.
cards.misconception: The Foundry project endpoint exposes embedding inference.
cards.volatilityNote: The project endpoint's supported inference routes can expand in later service or SDK releases.

cards.statement: For a repeatable release, a Foundry Agents v2 developer pins an agent reference to a specific version.
cards.explanation: A versioned agent reference lets a release call the intended agent definition even when newer versions exist.

cards.statement: Foundry migrates existing connection secrets when an engineer attaches their own Azure Key Vault.
cards.explanation: Foundry does not migrate connection secrets into a newly attached Azure Key Vault. The engineer recreates the connections afterward.
cards.misconception: Attaching a customer-managed vault migrates connection secrets.
cards.volatilityNote: Support for migrating existing secrets to a customer-managed vault can change.

source.title: Add a new connection to your project

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI can create separate quota pools per resource for the same subscription, region, model, and deployment type.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI shares quota across resources for the same subscription, region, model, and deployment type. Deployment allocations draw from that shared pool.
cards.misconception: Creating another Azure OpenAI resource creates an independent quota pool.

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI client can use retry-after-ms from a 429 response to schedule its next attempt.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI's retry-after-ms header supplies the wait before retrying. Honoring that interval helps a client avoid repeated throttling.

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI TPM enforcement uses the token count that Azure Monitor reports for billing.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI enforces TPM using a request-time estimate of potential token processing. Azure Monitor reports billed consumption after successful processing.
cards.misconception: Rate enforcement and billing use the same token count.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor lets an engineer split Azure OpenAI blocked-request metrics by content category.
cards.explanation: The Blocked Volume metric counts Azure OpenAI requests rejected by content filters. Its Category dimension helps an engineer identify the categories causing rejections.

cards.statement: Azure AI Search's top-level running status confirms that an indexer is executing its latest run.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search's top-level running status means the indexer is ready to execute. The execution result's status shows whether a particular run is active.
cards.misconception: An indexer's top-level status describes its current execution.

cards.statement: Azure AI Search includes document-specific indexing errors in an indexer's execution results.
cards.explanation: Azure AI Search records document-specific problems in the Errors and Warnings fields of indexer execution results. An engineer inspects those records to troubleshoot ingestion.

cards.statement: An administrator assigns Foundry User to a project's managed identity for Foundry resource access.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Foundry checks the project's managed identity as a separate caller. Foundry User on the Foundry resource authorizes that identity's project operations.

source.title: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Foundry Agent Consumer allows a service principal to edit agent definitions in a Foundry project.
cards.explanation: Foundry Agent Consumer grants a service principal access to invoke agent endpoints. Editing agent definitions requires a role with project development permissions.
cards.misconception: Permission to invoke an agent includes permission to edit its definition.

source.title: Role-based access control for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Azure Monitor's legacy Latency metric is designed to measure Azure OpenAI generation response time.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI provides Time to Last Byte for response latency. The legacy Cognitive Services Latency metric gives misleading results for Azure OpenAI workloads.
cards.misconception: The legacy Cognitive Services latency metric measures generative response latency accurately.

cards.statement: Foundry clients keep the same endpoint hostname when DNS routes requests through a private endpoint.
cards.explanation: Foundry clients retain their resource endpoint connection string for private access. DNS resolves that hostname to the private endpoint's IP address inside the connected virtual network.

source.title: Configure network isolation for Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 can return HTTP 400 with content_filter when the Responses API blocks a prompt.
cards.explanation: A blocked Azure OpenAI v1 Responses input raises BadRequestError in Python. The content_filter code identifies a guardrail rejection for the app to handle.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: A developer changes a Foundry model's default guardrail by editing its built-in policy.
cards.explanation: Microsoft's built-in default guardrail is read-only. A developer creates a custom guardrail and assigns it to the model deployment to change the safety policy.
cards.misconception: The built-in default policy is editable.

source.title: Configure guardrails and controls in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Prompt Shields uses its detected annotation to confirm that it blocks an attack.
cards.explanation: Prompt Shields reports detection and filtering separately. An app reads filtered to establish whether the detected attack was blocked.
cards.misconception: Detection confirms that the service blocks the attack.

cards.statement: Prompt Shields scans user prompts for attempts to replace the model's system instructions.
cards.explanation: Prompt Shields checks user input for attacks against system instructions or safety training. A request to adopt an unrestricted persona is one attack pattern.

cards.statement: Protected Material for Code returns source URLs when it finds matching code in GitHub repositories.
cards.explanation: Protected Material for Code includes codeCitations with sourceUrls for detected matches. An app uses those repository references to explain the match.

cards.statement: Foundry content safety evaluators use the developer's model deployment to score harmful response content.
cards.explanation: Foundry content safety evaluators use Microsoft's hosted safety models. Developers supply Foundry project information rather than a judge deployment_name.
cards.misconception: Safety evaluators use the application's model deployment as their judge.

cards.statement: Foundry safety evaluation results include a reason explaining the assigned harm severity.
cards.explanation: Foundry content safety evaluators return a severity score and an explanatory reason. The reason helps a developer understand the assigned score.

cards.statement: The Dataset evaluation target in Microsoft Foundry reruns the agent to produce responses.
cards.explanation: Foundry's Dataset evaluation scores responses already stored in the dataset. A developer selects this target to assess captured outputs.
cards.misconception: Evaluating saved responses reruns the original agent.

source.title: Run evaluations from the Microsoft Foundry portal

cards.statement: Foundry prompt-agent tracing can capture tool-call arguments when project tracing is enabled.
cards.explanation: Tool arguments can enter Foundry prompt-agent trace telemetry. Developers redact secrets and personal data before those values enter telemetry.
cards.appliesTo: Foundry Agents v2; prompt-agent server-side tracing

source.title: Set up tracing in Microsoft Foundry

cards.statement: Foundry Agents v2 toolboxes can use descriptions in allowed_tools to restrict MCP tool access.
cards.explanation: A toolbox's allowed_tools filter uses exact, case-sensitive tool names. Developers inspect tools/list and copy its names when configuring permitted tools.
cards.misconception: Tool descriptions identify entries in the allowlist.

source.title: Create and manage a toolbox in Foundry
